description: We are Team Asterix from Egypt. Our project. Our goal is to build, an interactive website that tells the story of equipment NASA left on the Moon and Mars for kids in a fun, story-driven way. Challenge #1 Abandoned but not Forgotten.
summary: ECHOES is a cinematic educational space game that transforms abandoned Moon and Mars missions into interactive stories. Built with Lovable, it features NASA-based facts, interactive maps, spacecraft exploration, missions, quizzes, and XP progression, inspiring beginners to discover humanity’s forgotten space history through accurate, immersive storytelling.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?
ECHOES is an interactive educational website about the spacecraft and rovers humanity has left on the Moon and Mars. Users choose a world, meet each machine through a story card, and locate it on a real NASA orbital map. A Discoveries page lists confirmed scientific results, each with a link to its NASA source. A built-in game lets players scan for signals, recover a machine, read its story, answer a question and earn XP, ranking up from Cadet to Echo Keeper.
What are the benefits?
It makes space history engaging for children, students and beginners by turning facts into a mission.
It is trustworthy, because every claim links to NASA records and unknown information is labeled instead of guessed.
It works in any browser and is responsive on desktop, tablet and mobile.
What is the intended impact?
We want to spark curiosity about space exploration and show that every mission, even one that has ended, still teaches us something. We also want to encourage the habit of checking sources. Because the site is built to be scalable, more missions can be added over time.
Tools, languages and software used
Languages and frameworks: TypeScript, React, TanStack Start, Tailwind CSS.
Mapping: Leaflet with real imagery from NASA Trek (LRO WAC Moon mosaic) and Mars Trek.
Data sources: NASA, NASA Image Library, NSSDCA, Moon Trek and Mars Trek.
Design: Custom dark space design system, Canvas-based starfield, and Michroma, Manrope and JetBrains Mono fonts.
Development and deployment: The AI builder Lovable, GitHub for version control, and Vercel for hosting.
Hardware: Standard laptop and web browser. No special hardware was required.
How is it creative?
Instead of a typical information website, ECHOES is designed like a cinematic space game. Forgotten machines become characters with stories, the map works as a discovery tool, and the game rewards curiosity rather than memorization. The visual identity combines a NASA-inspired look with a sci-fi game menu feel, and it avoids clutter and cartoon styling.
What factors did we consider?
Scientific accuracy: Only verified NASA information is used, with source links, and no invented dates, coordinates or discoveries.
Accessibility: The site is mobile-friendly, labels interactive elements, and respects reduced-motion settings.
Audience: Navigation and language are simple enough for beginners and children.
Performance: Images are optimized so the site loads quickly.
Transparency: The site states it is an independent educational project, not affiliated with NASA, and we used AI tools to help build it while we directed the concept, content and design.
dataRefs: The NSSDCA is NASA's definitive, publicly available catalog. Participants can use it to search for any spacecraft or instrument sent into space, retrieve its mission parameters, and learn exactly what its final resting place and operational status is.
